output.headline: Awards $101,854 to Deco Tech Systems for new security cameras at Lincoln Elementary
output.summary: The board is awarding the contract to Deco Tech Systems, Inc. as the lowest responsive, responsible bidder and rejecting all other bids. The company will install about 20 new security cameras, troubleshoot one existing camera, supply about 3 spare cameras and replace the camera recording server at Lincoln Elementary School. The contract is $101,854.00, including a $9,000.00 contingency allowance, and the text says work was expected to start August 27, 2026, before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Consolidated Engineering Laboratories up to $7,656 for more soil consulting at Garfield school site
output.summary: Consolidated Engineering Laboratories will provide further geotechnical (soil and ground) consultation for the Garfield Elementary School Site New Construction Project. This includes engineer meetings and analysis, and compaction testing of backfill, as described in a proposal dated May 28, 2026. The not-to-exceed amount is $7,656.00, including a $696.00 contingency fee for additional services, and the work lasts for the duration of the project.

output.headline: Adds $823 for inspection services on Markham Elementary boys' toilet room renovation
output.summary: King Construction Inspection, Inc. will provide additional inspection services for the Markham Elementary School Boys Toilet Room Renovation Project. This amendment adds $823.00, raising the not-to-exceed amount of the agreement from $7,832.00 to $8,655.00. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies no-cost Stanford partnership on multilingual math talk, with a data sharing agreement
output.summary: Stanford Graduate School of Education will work with OUSD teachers on their own goals through co-planning sessions, and give the district de-identified information about multilingual learners' math language practices and open-source tools to assess student math talk. A separate Data Sharing Agreement sets the terms for the district sharing pupil data with Stanford and how that data is protected. Both run January 30 through December 31, 2026 at no cost to the district.

vendor.name: Board of Trustees of Stanford University

output.headline: Ratifies up to $42,000 for Smartcat translation software and services
output.summary: Smartcat Platform, Inc. will provide subscription services and translation services as described in an order form, through the Special Education Department. The period is July 14, 2026 through July 13, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $42,000.00. The official text does not say which materials will be translated.

output.headline: Approves up to $70,000 for Invo Healthcare to staff mental health services for students with IEPs
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The stated not-to-exceed amount of $70,000.00 looks small for the staffing described over nearly three years; the amount may be misprinted or may cover only part of the cost.
output.summary: Invo Healthcare Associates, LLC will provide seven full-time mental health clinicians, seven full-time mental/behavioral health technicians, one therapeutic behavior support provider and a program supervisor. They will give counseling required by students' Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) at schools, in the community or at home. A separate data sharing agreement covers protection of student data. The term is August 5, 2026 through June 30, 2029, with an amount not to exceed $70,000.00.

output.headline: Approves up to $180,000 for YouthBeat after-school music and digital arts at 11 schools
output.summary: YouthBeat will run after-school music and digital arts enrichment at 11 school sites, up to two days a week with up to 20 students per class. Up to 200 students are expected to receive 1,200 hours of free digital arts instruction during the year. The period is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $180,000.00.

output.headline: Adds $43,077 to keep Deco Tech's security camera and door entry maintenance running
output.summary: This change order adds general maintenance services to continue the ongoing maintenance of security cameras and door entry systems at various sites. It raises the contract price from $520,850.00 to $563,927.00, an increase of $43,077.00. All other terms of the agreement stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $80,000 for East Bay Art Therapy's after-school group therapy at four schools
output.summary: East Bay Art Therapy will provide after-school, arts-based group therapy at four elementary and continuation school sites, at least one day a week per site, with up to 10 students per session. It is meant to reach up to 85 students for a total of 120 hours of free art therapy. The period is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $80,000.00.

output.headline: Adds $11,796 for concrete, toilet, conduit and lighting work at Markham Elementary restroom
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text calls the extension from July 31, 2026 to August 21, 2026 twenty-three calendar days, but those dates are 21 days apart.
output.summary: This change order with Next Generation of Builders, LLC covers added work on the Markham Elementary School Boys Toilet Renovation Project: replacing a concrete slab found in poor condition, repairing a damaged toilet flange, adding ceiling conduit supports and upgrading light fixtures. The net addition is $11,796.39 after applying $1,040.09 of pending allowance funds, raising the contract from $238,475.00 to $250,271.39. It also extends the end date to August 21, 2026.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $100,000 for Destiny Arts Center visual and performing arts at five schools
output.summary: Destiny Arts Center will provide visual and performing arts programming at five school sites, with up to 20 students per class and classes twice a week over a 30-week program. About 150 students are expected to receive a total of 1,200 hours of arts instruction. The period is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $100,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for CloudBase to upgrade the Summer Learning timekeeping and payroll platform
output.summary: CloudBase Services will make targeted improvements to the district's existing Summer Learning platform, including timekeeping, payroll preparation, reporting and workflow automation. The changes build on lessons from the 2026 Summer Learning Program. The period is August 1 through September 30, 2026, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $50,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $75,000 for Dimensions Dance Theatre out-of-school dance classes at three schools
output.summary: Dimensions Dance Theatre will teach cultural dance styles of the African Diaspora and world cultures to students at three school sites during out-of-school hours. Classes run up to 2 days a week with up to 20 students per class over 30 weeks, for 720 hours. The period is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $75,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $53,060 for Scientific Adventures for Girls' after-school STEM program
output.summary: Scientific Adventures for Girls will provide hands-on science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) enrichment for up to 180 elementary school girls at two school sites. Weekly after-school sessions run for 24 weeks, led by STEM educators with teaching assistants, near-peer mentors and volunteers. The period is September 1, 2026 through May 31, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $53,060.00.

output.headline: Approves up to $90,000 for HERO's structured recess and leadership program at Laurel Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program at Laurel Elementary School with active supervision and organized games, aimed at student engagement, fewer conflicts and a safe, inclusive playground. Upper-grade students will also take part in the Young HERO Program, a daily leadership initiative with monthly workshops. The period is August 10, 2026 through June 25, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $90,000.00.

output.headline: Approves up to $132,000 for East Bay Agency for Children mental health support at Rudsdale High
output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children will provide 40 hours a week of clinical mental health support to students at Rudsdale Continuation High School. It will also provide training classes for school staff clinicians, 4.5 hours of consultation, and a clinical supervisor who attends team meetings and three additional annual meetings with the principal or designee. The period is July 13, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $132,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $105,000 for Public Profit to evaluate 84 expanded learning programs
output.summary: Public Profit will evaluate the district's 84 Expanded Learning Programs, including reviewing after-school documentation, creating and sending student and family surveys, and holding four meetings with 130 site coordinators and agency directors on using data. Each school site will also get a program profile with its own data. The period is July 15, 2026 through June 30, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $105,000.00.

output.headline: Cuts $2.02M from Syserco's CAL Shape design-build contract, lowering it to $7.8M
output.summary: Change Order No. 6 reduces the Syserco Energy Solutions, Inc. design-build contract for the CAL Shape project by a net $2,021,327.02, from $9,837,080.68 to $7,815,753.66. The main change is a $2,033,894.75 deduction across 78 OUSD sites to reflect work actually completed compared with initial estimates. Small additions cover extra repairs at one school and extra cost for installing CO2 sensors during second shift in active classrooms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $32,000 for a contractor to run weekly food bank distributions at Rudsdale High
output.summary: An individual contractor will coordinate weekly food bank procurement and distribution at Rudsdale Continuation High School, including ordering, pick-up, set-up, student intern facilitation and clean-up. About 2,500 pounds of fresh and non-perishable food will be distributed weekly during the school year and summer school, plus 4 special event distributions. The period is August 1, 2026 through May 28, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $32,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Cantare Con Vivo music classes at La Escuelita Elementary
output.summary: Cantare Con Vivo will teach music classes at La Escuelita Elementary School focused on music fundamentals, community and teamwork. The provider will plan a standards-based curriculum, work with classroom teachers and finish with a performance showcase for the school community and families. The period is August 11, 2026 through May 27, 2027, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $5,000.00.

output.headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $48,300 for soccer and wellness support at Rudsdale

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $48,300.00

output.summary: Soccer Without Borders will serve 60 students at Rudsdale Continuation High School with weekly practices, coaching, mentorship and league play, and will cover uniforms, equipment, league fees and transportation support. The agreement runs August 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies no-cost therapy services from Fred Finch Youth & Family Services at Garfield Elementary
output.summary: Fred Finch Youth & Family Services will provide therapeutic services for students at Garfield Elementary School, including individual, group and family therapy, crisis intervention, workshops and psychoeducation. The period is August 10, 2026 through May 31, 2027, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for a contractor's computer and printing support at Edna Brewer Middle School
output.summary: An individual contractor will provide technical support for Windows and Apple Macintosh computers at Edna Brewer Middle School, including maintaining and improving the school network, improving classroom and lab printing, and building a reliable printing solution for staff and student Chromebooks. The period is August 1 through September 15, 2026, which began before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $5,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies $7,974 for Vik Staffing's event support at the New Teacher Institute
output.summary: Vik Staffing provided on-site event support for the New Teacher Institute, including breakfast and lunch setup, bussing services and general assistance for new teachers, staff and facilitators. The service period was July 27 through July 31, 2026, which was before this vote. The amount is not to exceed $7,974.00.

output.headline: Pays Shred Works up to $12,000 to shred confidential documents at central offices

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $12,000.00

output.summary: Shred Works will shred confidential documents throughout the district's central offices. The agreement runs August 7, 2026 to May 31, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $11,680 for Cooperative Personnel Services to study job classifications
output.summary: Cooperative Personnel Services will study how district jobs are classified. The work includes reviewing job questionnaires, interviewing employees and supervisors, recommending changes to existing job specifications and writing new ones where needed. The period is July 22, 2026 through June 30, 2027, starting before this vote, and the amount is not to exceed $11,680.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,000 for a consultant to build college partnerships for teacher recruitment
output.summary: An education consulting company will develop and maintain partnerships with colleges and universities to support new teacher recruitment. The work includes drafting and negotiating memorandums of understanding (MOUs) with those schools, getting legal department approval and tracking each one through the Talent/Human Resources approval process. The period is August 10, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the amount is not to exceed $12,000.00.

vendor.name: William L. Winston, Education Consulting LLC

output.headline: Ratifies up to $8,000 for Urban Leader Coaching to support reading instruction at Allendale Elementary
output.summary: Urban Leader Coaching, LLC will coach the principal and the Teacher on Special Assignment (TSA) at Allendale Elementary School on coaching teachers in reading instruction. Virtual 60-minute sessions will cover data review and putting instructional strategies into practice. The period is August 17, 2026 through April 30, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $8,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $58,598 for SEAL to deliver early learning trainings for the district
output.summary: Sobrato Early Academic Language (SEAL) will provide up to two qualified presenters to deliver four of the Designs for Change Four-Day Early Learning Series during 2026-2027, as described in an attached exhibit, through the Early Childhood Development Department. The period is August 17, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $58,598.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $23,102 for Wellness Together counseling support at Urban Promise Academy
output.summary: Wellness Together will provide a consultant for counseling support at Urban Promise Academy, including individual and group counseling, family engagement sessions, classroom presentations and up to three referrals to community mental health providers when school-based services end. It will also give the school aggregate data that does not identify individual students. The period is August 10, 2026 through May 31, 2027 and the amount is not to exceed $23,102.00.

output.headline: Community Resources for Science gives free science teaching support to all OUSD elementary schools
output.summary: Community Resources For Science, a Berkeley nonprofit partner, will lead science lessons in classrooms and offer teachers resources, training and planning help at no cost to the district. The support covers all elementary schools and runs from September 10, 2026 to May 30, 2027. This is a no-cost partnership agreement.

output.headline: Bay Area Creative offers free poetry and literature workshops at Franklin Elementary
output.summary: Bay Area Creative will hold poetry and literature workshops for students at Franklin Elementary School to build vocabulary, reading fluency and phonological awareness (hearing the sounds in words). It costs the district nothing. The agreement period began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $255,000 for tobacco and drug prevention coaches

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $255,000.00

output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will hire Tobacco Use Prevention Education coaches who work one-on-one with students, lead small drug-intervention groups, and do school outreach. Each coach would manage a caseload of up to 10 students per school. The agreement runs August 10, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Trybe offers a free after-school drop-in center and mentoring; student data sharing included
output.summary: Trybe, Inc. will run an after-school drop-in program at San Antonio Park Courts with college and career mentoring for students, mainly from Roosevelt Middle, Garfield Elementary and Oakland High. A separate data-sharing agreement sets rules for how the district shares student information with Trybe and how Trybe protects it. Both run August 13, 2026 to August 12, 2027 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves Personnel Report No. 2627-0001 from Talent/Human Resources
output.summary: The board is asked to approve Personnel Report No. 2627-0001 from the Talent/Human Resources Department. The official text does not list the individual personnel actions or any dollar amounts, which are in the report itself.

output.headline: Pays a science assistant up to $34,200 to support hands-on science at Chabot Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $34,200.00

output.summary: A contractor will help K-5 teachers set up science experiments, deliver hands-on lessons, manage supplies, and organize the school science fair at Chabot Elementary School. The agreement runs August 5, 2026 to June 30, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Sets up a five-year no-cost agreement with Smith College to place social work students in district schools
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) lets Smith College's School for Social Work place graduate students in district schools for practicum experience, including Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) credentials such as school social work. It runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 at no cost to the district. Some non-teaching interns who are not district employees may receive stipends drawn from nonprofit grants to the district, such as from the Ed Fund.

output.headline: Pays The Finer Print up to $5,500 for design of the updated crisis response manual

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,500.00

output.summary: The Finer Print will provide up to 35 hours of graphic design and layout for the district's updated Crisis Response Manual, which covers responses to student mental health crises, including police-free responses. The work period was July 15 to August 1, 2026, before this board vote.

output.headline: Accelerating Literacy Leadership Institute gives free literacy support; student data sharing included
output.summary: Accelerating Literacy Leadership Institute will provide literacy support to schools and central district teams at no cost. A separate data-sharing agreement sets rules for how the district shares student information with the group and how the group protects it. Both run August 13, 2026 to August 13, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Genesys Works Bay Area offers free career internships and training for high school students
output.summary: Genesys Works Bay Area will provide skills training, internships and work experience for eligible high school students in underserved communities, through the High School Linked Learning Office. It costs the district nothing. The agreement runs April 30, 2026 to January 1, 2029 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $45,000 for structured recess and student leaders at Think College Now

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00

output.summary: HERO will run structured recess and lunch recess activities and train student leaders to reduce conflicts and build belonging at Think College Now Elementary School. The agreement runs August 10, 2026 to May 27, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $119,000 to coordinate mental health support at child development centers

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $119,000.00

output.summary: A contractor will coordinate early childhood mental health services across 17 district Child Development Centers, coach educators, run parent workshops, and help connect families to outside services. The agreement runs August 24, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays Ball for Life Oakland up to $35,000 for physical education and recess at Reach Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $35,000.00

output.summary: Ball for Life Oakland LLC will run a structured physical education and recess program with organized games and active supervision at Reach Academy. The agreement runs August 10, 2026 to May 27, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: HERO provides a free structured recess program at Cleveland Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program at Cleveland Elementary School to improve student engagement, reduce conflicts and create a safe playground, at no cost to the district. The agreement runs August 10, 2026 to May 27, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $45,000 for structured recess and leadership program at Horace Mann Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00

output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program with active supervision and conflict resolution, plus a daily leadership program for upper-grade students, at Horace Mann Elementary School. The agreement runs August 10, 2026 to May 27, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $58,800 for structured recess and leadership program at Hoover Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $58,800.00

output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program, a daily leadership program for upper-grade students, and monthly leadership workshops at Hoover Elementary School. The agreement runs August 10, 2026 to May 27, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Agency for Children up to $60,000 for a Spanish-speaking counselor at Greenleaf

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00

output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children will provide a bilingual Spanish mental health provider who meets weekly, one on one, with a caseload of 10 to 15 students at Greenleaf Elementary School. The agreement runs August 24, 2026 to May 27, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Connected Minds Consulting Group up to $10,000 for an early childhood educator training day

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: Connected Minds Consulting Group, LLC will deliver a full-day professional learning institute for early childhood educators, with a keynote and two learning sessions on belonging, anti-bias education and family partnerships. The agreement runs August 17, 2026 to June 30, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Navalta Media up to $114,000 for strategic communications and media relations

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $114,000.00

output.summary: Navalta Media will provide strategic communications, media relations, reputation management and executive communications support for the district. The agreement runs July 22, 2026 to May 22, 2027 and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Declares district vehicles surplus and authorizes their disposal
output.summary: This resolution declares certain district vehicles obsolete and surplus and lets the district dispose of them. The text states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Updates dental plan agreement with Self-Insured Schools of California on outside vendors
output.summary: The district's dental plan agreement with Self Insured Schools of California is updated so the district cannot contract with outside companies that handle electronic eligibility data without the plan's approval and a signed business associate agreement. The change takes effect July 1, 2026, and all other terms of the 2014 agreement stay the same.

output.headline: Approves minutes of the Board's August 24, 2026 special meeting
output.summary: The Board of Education ratifies the written minutes of its special meeting held on August 24, 2026. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Approves minutes of the Board's August 26, 2026 regular meeting
output.summary: The Board of Education ratifies the written minutes of its regular meeting held on August 26, 2026. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.
